title: A Single Cloud Can Weigh Over a Million Pounds
description: That fluffy cloud floating above you holds an astonishing amount of water. Here is how it stays up.

scenes.text: That soft little cloud floating above you could weigh more than a million pounds.
Clouds are made of countless tiny water droplets. A typical puffy cloud can hold around five hundred tons of water.
So why doesn't it crash down? Because that weight is spread across a huge space, and each droplet is incredibly small.
The droplets are so light that rising warm air keeps them floating, until they join together and fall as rain.
So the next time you look up, remember there are elephants worth of water up there. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Lightning Is Hotter Than the Surface of the Sun
description: A bolt of lightning heats the air around it to about five times the temperature of the Sun's surface.

scenes.text: Every bolt of lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Lightning can heat the air around it to roughly thirty thousand degrees Celsius, in a fraction of a second.
The surface of the Sun is about five and a half thousand degrees. So lightning is around five times hotter.
That sudden heat makes the air expand explosively. The boom you hear is thunder.
A tiny piece of something hotter than the Sun, right outside your window. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Koala Fingerprints Look Almost Exactly Like Ours
description: Koalas have fingerprints so similar to human ones that they are hard to tell apart, even under a microscope.

scenes.text: Koalas have fingerprints. And they look almost exactly like ours.
They have the same loops, arches and swirls that we have on our fingertips.
Scientists have said that even under a microscope, koala prints can be very hard to tell apart from human ones.
Koalas are not close relatives of ours. Their prints probably developed to help them grip branches and handle their leafy food.
Nature sometimes solves the same problem twice. Follow for more weird facts.

title: The Eiffel Tower Grows Taller in Summer
description: The iron tower in Paris expands in the heat and can stand about fifteen centimeters taller on hot days.

scenes.text: The Eiffel Tower gets taller every summer.
It is built from iron, and metal expands when it heats up.
On hot days, the tower can grow by up to about fifteen centimeters. That is about six inches.
And because the Sun heats one side more than the other, the top can lean slightly away from the Sun during the day.
In winter, it shrinks back down again. Follow for more weird facts.

title: A Group of Flamingos Is Called a Flamboyance
description: Flamingos have one of the best group names in nature, and their pink color comes from what they eat.

scenes.text: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance. Honestly, it fits.
But here is the surprise. Flamingos are not born pink. The chicks are gray and white.
They turn pink from their food. Tiny shrimp and algae they eat contain natural pigments that color their feathers.
If a flamingo stops eating those foods, its feathers slowly fade to a paler color.
So the pinkest flamingo is simply the best fed. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Saturn Would Float in a Giant Bathtub
description: Saturn is the only planet in our solar system less dense than water.

scenes.text: If you could find a bathtub big enough, Saturn would float in it.
Saturn is enormous. More than seven hundred Earths could fit inside it. But it is mostly hydrogen and helium gas.
That makes it the only planet in our solar system that is less dense than water, on average.
Of course, no such bathtub exists, and the planet would not stay in one piece. But on paper, it floats.
A giant that weighs less than it looks. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Sea Otters Hold Hands While They Sleep
description: Sea otters sleep floating on their backs, and they often hold on to each other so they don't drift apart.

scenes.text: Sea otters often hold hands while they sleep.
They sleep floating on their backs in the ocean, which means the waves could easily carry them away.
So they grab on to each other's paws, forming little groups that stay together through the night.
Some also wrap themselves in long strands of seaweed, like a blanket that keeps them in place.
The ocean's cutest sleepover. Follow for more weird facts.

title: A Blue Whale's Heart Weighs as Much as Two People
description: The largest animal ever has a heart to match, and its heartbeat can be detected from far away.

scenes.text: The blue whale is the largest animal that has ever lived, and its heart is enormous.
A blue whale's heart can weigh around one hundred and eighty kilograms. That is about the weight of two grown adults.
When it dives, that heart can slow down to just two beats per minute, to save oxygen.
Scientists only recorded a wild blue whale's heartbeat for the first time in twenty nineteen, using a sensor stuck on with suction cups.
The biggest heart on the planet belongs to a gentle giant. Follow for more weird facts.

title: The Largest Desert on Earth Is Covered in Ice
description: A desert is defined by how little rain or snow it gets, not by heat. That makes Antarctica the biggest one.

scenes.text: The largest desert in the world is not hot or sandy. It is Antarctica.
A desert is any place that gets very little rain or snow each year. Heat has nothing to do with it.
The middle of Antarctica gets less yearly snowfall than many famous hot deserts get in rain.
The ice is there because it almost never melts. It has built up slowly over hundreds of thousands of years.
The driest continent is also the coldest. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Earth Has More Trees Than the Milky Way Has Stars
description: Scientists estimate there are about three trillion trees on Earth, far more than the stars in our galaxy.

scenes.text: There are more trees on Earth than stars in our galaxy.
A large study estimated there are about three trillion trees on our planet.
The Milky Way is thought to have somewhere between one hundred and four hundred billion stars.
The same study found that billions of trees are cut down every year, so that number keeps shrinking.
Every one of those trees counts. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Everest Isn't the Tallest Mountain on Earth
description: Everest has the highest peak above sea level, but another mountain is taller from base to top.

scenes.text: Mount Everest is not the tallest mountain on Earth. It is just the highest.
Everest's peak is the highest point above sea level, at almost eight thousand eight hundred and fifty meters.
But in Hawaii there is a volcano called Mauna Kea. Most of it is hidden under the ocean.
Measured from its base on the sea floor to its top, Mauna Kea is more than ten thousand meters tall.
It depends on where you start measuring. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Scotland's National Animal Is the Unicorn
description: Scotland chose a mythical creature as its national animal, and it has been a symbol there for centuries.

scenes.text: The national animal of Scotland is the unicorn.
It has been a Scottish symbol for hundreds of years, and it appeared on the royal coat of arms.
In old stories, the unicorn stood for purity, strength and pride, and it was said that only a king could tame one.
Many old carvings show the unicorn in chains, a sign of how wild and powerful it was believed to be.
A real country, with an imaginary animal. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Napoleon Wasn't Actually Short
description: The idea that Napoleon was tiny is a myth that came from a measurement mix up and wartime cartoons.

scenes.text: Napoleon is famous for being short. But he probably wasn't.
Most historians think he was around one point seven meters tall, roughly average for a Frenchman of his time.
Part of the confusion came from measurements. French inches were longer than British inches, so his height sounded smaller than it was.
British cartoonists also loved drawing him as a tiny, angry man, and the image stuck.
Sometimes history remembers the joke, not the truth. Follow for more weird facts.

title: The Shortest War in History Lasted Under an Hour
description: In 1896, a war between Britain and Zanzibar was over in less than an hour.

scenes.text: The shortest war in recorded history lasted less than an hour.
It happened in eighteen ninety six, between Britain and Zanzibar, an island off the coast of East Africa.
A new sultan took power without British approval. Britain gave him a deadline to step down, and he refused.
When the deadline passed, British ships opened fire. The fighting ended in roughly forty minutes.
Shorter than most movies. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Water Can Boil and Freeze at the Same Time
description: At one special temperature and pressure, water can be solid, liquid and gas all at once.

scenes.text: Water can boil and freeze at the exact same time.
It happens at something called the triple point, where ice, liquid water and water vapor can all exist together.
It needs a temperature just above zero degrees Celsius, and a pressure far lower than the air around us.
In a lab with a vacuum pump, you can watch water bubble like it is boiling while ice forms on top.
Water is weirder than it looks. Follow for more weird facts.

title: This Frog Turns See-Through When It Sleeps
description: Glass frogs hide almost all their red blood cells in their liver while sleeping, becoming nearly invisible.

scenes.text: There is a frog that can make itself almost see-through. It is called the glass frog.
Glass frogs live in rainforests in Central and South America, and the skin on their bellies is clear.
Scientists found that when they sleep, these frogs pack most of their red blood cells into their liver.
With their red blood tucked away, they become two to three times more transparent, and much harder for predators to spot.
Its own built in invisibility trick. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Tiny Water Bears Have Survived Outer Space
description: Tardigrades are microscopic animals tough enough to survive being exposed to space.

scenes.text: There is a tiny animal that has survived a trip into outer space. It is the tardigrade, also called the water bear.
Tardigrades are smaller than a millimeter long and live almost everywhere, even in the moss on a garden wall.
In two thousand seven, scientists sent some into orbit and exposed them to the vacuum of space. Some survived and even had babies afterward.
When conditions get harsh, they dry out and curl up into a tiny ball, almost shutting down their bodies until things get better.
The toughest animal on Earth might be living in your garden. Follow for more weird facts.

title: Spider Silk Is Stronger Than Steel
description: Ounce for ounce, some spider silk is stronger than steel, and it can stretch too.

scenes.text: Spider silk can be stronger than steel.
Compared weight for weight, some kinds of spider silk are stronger than steel.
Unlike steel, it can also stretch a long way before it breaks. That is why a web can stop a flying insect without snapping.
Researchers have spent years trying to copy it, for things like medical stitches and lightweight protective gear.
One of the strongest materials on Earth is spun by a spider. Follow for more weird facts.

title: The Sunlight You See Is 8 Minutes Old
description: Light takes time to travel, so when you look at the Sun you are seeing it as it was about eight minutes ago.

scenes.text: The sunlight hitting your face right now left the Sun about eight minutes ago.
The Sun is about one hundred and fifty million kilometers away. Even light needs time to cross that distance.
Traveling at the speed of light, it takes around eight minutes and twenty seconds to reach us.
So you always see the Sun as it was, not as it is. And for distant stars, that light can be thousands of years old.
Every time you look up, you are looking back in time. Follow for more weird facts.

title: This Shrimp Snaps Hard Enough to Create Heat Like the Sun
description: The pistol shrimp snaps its claw so fast that it makes a bubble that briefly gets incredibly hot.

scenes.text: There is a shrimp with a claw that works like a weapon. It is called the pistol shrimp.
It snaps its claw shut so quickly that it shoots out a jet of water and creates a tiny bubble.
When that bubble collapses, the inside briefly reaches thousands of degrees, close to the temperature of the Sun's surface.
The snap is also one of the loudest sounds in the ocean, and it can stun small fish nearby.
Small shrimp, huge power. Follow for more weird facts.
